title: the Sri Yantra
hook: can a drawing be a home for the divine?
tomorrow: a wall around a home, with a gate in every side. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Vijnana Bhairava closed: worship turned inward, and the Goddess's embrace. Today, the Goddess again, this time drawn in lines.
screen: `WORSHIP WAS NEVER ONLY ON THE SHELF.`

segments.voice: Unpacking a home shrine, things come out of the newspaper one at a time: a lamp, a bell, a small framed picture of a god. Then a flat brass plate with no face on it at all. Just lines: triangles crossing triangles, rings of petals, a square border with a gate on each side, and a tiny point in the middle. And it gets the same flowers as everything else on the shelf. So, one question for today: can a drawing be a home for the divine?
screen: `OUT OF THE NEWSPAPER.` → `A PLATE WITH NO FACE.` → `CAN A DRAWING BE A HOME?`

segments.voice: This is the Sri Yantra, also called the Sri Chakra. A yantra is a diagram used in worship and meditation, and this one is at the heart of Sri Vidya, a way of worship centered on the Goddess as Lalita Tripurasundari. Her thousand names, the Lalita Sahasranama, include one that answers today's question: she is the one whose home is the Sri Chakra, king of chakras. So for those who worship with it, the yantra isn't decoration, and it isn't a reminder of someone absent. It's treated as her dwelling and her form, drawn in geometry instead of painted with a face. A neighbor tradition asks a close cousin of this question. In the book of Exodus, read by Jews and Christians, God tells Moses: "And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them." Then God shows Moses a pattern, and the tabernacle is built to it, measure by measure. Here's what the two share: a made thing, built with care to a given design, as a place where the holy is among people. And the honest difference. In Exodus, nothing in the sanctuary is made to be God's form; the commandments say, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image." In Sri Vidya, the lines themselves are honored as the Goddess's form. Two old answers to one question, each in its own words.
screen: `THE SRI YANTRA: HER HOME AND FORM.` · `EXODUS: A SANCTUARY TO DWELL IN.` · `SHARED: A MADE PLACE FOR THE HOLY.` · `DIFFERENT: FORM, OR NO IMAGE.` · then, large: `A HOME DRAWN IN LINES.`

segments.voice: If there's paper and a pen nearby, draw a small square, a triangle inside it, and a dot at the center, slowly, with no need to be neat. Then rest your eyes on the dot for the rest of the sit. If you pray, you can let the drawing be a small place for the one you pray to; if not, let it be a place for your attention to come home.
The Sri Yantra: a diagram of lines, honored in Sri Vidya as the Goddess's own home and form.
Your line: the Sri Yantra, a home drawn in lines. A new run starts here.
